title: Arrangers and how arrangements were made
summary: They discuss Rosie McCarr and arrangers like Dave Rose, and how few players made charts in small bands compared with now.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And did you work with Rosie McCarr over there?
Rosie was in the band? Rosie used to make mouthpieces for me. Oh, yeah? Yeah, crumbling, trumpet and... I didn't know he did that.
I know he arranged. Who were some of the good arrangers that you worked with? Worked with me?
Well, I'll tell you, like Dave Rose. Mm-hmm. Dave Rose and Elmer Schoeman and a few other guys, but I had a few of them that I can't remember the names.

Yeah. But you see, when I played with bands like Will Osborne and Elbert Knuck, like they had two saxophone players to make an arrangement, the piano player would make an arrangement. Everybody would, you know, get 10, 15 ocks to make a whole arrangement.
That's all. And 12, 15 pieces. At that time, period. Now it's in the hundreds, you know.
In those days, the arrangers didn't make one. Yeah.
